title: Big Orders with Customer Names
prompt:
Tables `customers(id, name)` and `orders(id, customer_id, amount)`.

Return the order `id`, the customer's `name`, and the `amount` for every order with `amount` greater than 100.
hint: JOIN orders to customers on customer_id = customers.id, filter amount > 100.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER);

tests.seed_sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,150),(2,2,50),(3,1,90);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Cara'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,200),(2,1,300);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Dan'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,10);

title: Top Earner in Each Department
prompt:
Table `employees(id, name, dept, salary)`. Assume no salary ties within a department.

Return the `dept` and `name` of the highest-paid employee in each department.
hint: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC), then filter rank = 1.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER);

title: Customers Without Orders
prompt:
Tables `customers(id, name)` and `orders(id, customer_id)`.

Return the `name` of every customer who has never placed an order.
hint: WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders), or a LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER);

tests.seed_sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Cara'),(2,'Dan'),(3,'Eve'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1),(2,3);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Fay'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1);
